mainEntity.name: How long do partial dentures last?

acceptedAnswer.text: The lifespan of partial dentures varies depending on the material, how well they are cared for, and changes in your oral health over time. Acrylic dentures may last around five to eight years, while cobalt-chrome dentures can often last longer with proper maintenance. Individual longevity will depend on clinical factors and how well the denture is maintained. However, the shape of your gums and jawbone changes gradually, which means all dentures will eventually need relining, adjusting, or replacing. Regular dental check-ups allow your dentist to monitor the fit and condition of your denture and advise when any changes are needed.

mainEntity.name: Can I eat normally with partial dentures?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most patients find they can eat a wide range of foods comfortably once they have adjusted to wearing their partial denture. It is usually advisable to start with softer foods and gradually introduce firmer items as you gain confidence. Cutting food into smaller pieces and chewing on both sides of the mouth can help distribute forces evenly. Very hard or sticky foods may pose a risk of dislodging or damaging the denture, so some caution is sensible. Your dentist can offer personalised dietary guidance based on your specific denture design.

mainEntity.name: Are partial dentures noticeable to other people?

acceptedAnswer.text: Modern partial dentures are designed to look as natural as possible. Flexible dentures with tooth-coloured clasps tend to be the least noticeable. Acrylic dentures can also be made to match the shade of your natural teeth and gums closely. Cobalt-chrome dentures may have visible metal clasps in certain positions, although careful design can minimise their appearance. During your consultation, you can discuss aesthetic preferences with your dentist so the final result meets your expectations as closely as possible.

mainEntity.name: Do I need to remove my partial dentures at night?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is generally recommended to remove partial dentures at night to give your gums and supporting tissues a period of rest. Wearing dentures continuously can increase the risk of fungal infections such as denture stomatitis and may contribute to accelerated bone resorption. Soaking your dentures overnight in water or a denture-cleaning solution also helps maintain their shape and hygiene. Your dentist can provide specific guidance based on your individual circumstances.

mainEntity.name: How do I know which type of partial denture is right for me?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most appropriate type of partial denture depends on several factors, including the number and position of your missing teeth, the health of your remaining teeth and gums, your budget, and your personal preferences. A thorough clinical examination and discussion with your dentist is the best way to determine which option suits your needs. During this assessment, your dentist can explain the advantages and limitations of each type and help you make an informed decision.

mainEntity.name: Can partial dentures be repaired if they break?

acceptedAnswer.text: In many cases, yes. Acrylic dentures can often be repaired relatively easily and affordably by a dental laboratory. Flexible dentures can be more challenging to repair due to the nature of the material. Cobalt-chrome dentures may require more specialist repair work depending on the type of damage. It is important not to attempt repairs at home using household adhesives, as these can contain harmful chemicals and may make professional repair more difficult. If your denture breaks or becomes damaged, contact your dental practice for advice.
